title: "Driven Modal"
description: "Calculate modal RF response of the selected finite-ground CPW coupon."

---

## Purpose and selected system

Calculate reflection, transmission and fields when the selected port mode
excites the finite-ground CPW coupon. The layout is a straight Signal between
two finite Ground conductors, above a substrate, with exterior port cuts.
Use the notebook's exact section and length rather than a new generic CPW.

Modal is a solution kind, not another name for Wave excitation.
[Terminal response](driven-terminal.qmd) has a distinct conductor-reference
interpretation.

## Model and excitation choices

Specify conductor connectivity, materials, metal representation, physical Z,
substrate extent and the surrounding region. Preserve the exterior boundary
treatment and the port cuts.

For each port, retain its ordering, sheet extent, normal, integration-line
endpoints/direction, requested mode and normalization. De-embedding and
renormalization must remain explicit. A layout locator is not native port
readback.

The adaptive setup frequency and the output sweep have different purposes.
Mesh and pass controls govern adaptation; the sweep type/range/sample settings
govern reported response. Exact values and field-saving choices belong to
the notebook, with no duplicate numerical recipe here.

## Workflow

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Palace

A comparison using Palace must identify its own excitation basis, boundary
treatment and S-data convention. It is not automatically an HFSS Modal
calculation because the CPW source is shared.

### AEDT

Use [Finite CPW HFSS Driven Modal](../../notebooks/ComponentSimulation/CpwFiniteGround/aedt_hfss_driven_modal.ipynb).
Construct and inspect the native coupon, materials and port integration lines.
Solve the adaptive setup and requested sweep, then resolve returned data
independently of the live model session.

:::

## Expected outputs

Retain native port geometry and solved port-mode information, applied setup,
mesh/adaptive history and actual sweep samples. Return modal S-data and
requested magnitude/phase or field views with port/mode ordering and
normalization.

::: {.callout-note}
A response comparison must preserve each model's material, exterior and port
conventions. Similar plots do not alone establish equivalent physical models
or numerical accuracy.
:::
